inFlow stays your system of record: inFlow remains where your customer list, stock levels, lot tracking and invoices are kept. We look after every account's order guide, at prices you update in our web admin, and the orders their chefs send from the app.

Showroom shoppers can keep shopping: Customers who like browsing pictures and checking out online can stay on the Showroom. Our app is built for the kitchens that pick up the phone. A call that still comes in gets no number from us; in the app, each order is numbered and timed.

Restocking still runs on inFlow's reorder points: Its reorder points and suggested purchase orders still guide when you buy. We never raise purchase orders; we only bring in what each restaurant orders.

@graph.name: From inFlow export to first spoken order
@graph.description: Your part is one export out of inFlow; loading guides and opening accounts is ours.

step.name: Send us an inFlow export
step.text: A spreadsheet listing what every account orders and pays, with your own codes, is usually all we need.

step.name: Guides loaded, accounts opened
step.text: We load each guide and open its account. The chef downloads the app, and most kitchens send a first order the same day.

step.name: Orders arrive already checked
step.text: Each arrives reviewed by the kitchen, numbered, timed and in the format you chose.

@graph.name: Is an inFlow Inventory alternative the only way to get kitchens speaking their orders?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. inFlow stays, Showroom stays for those who enjoy shopping, and the restaurants still on the phone with you get our app. You receive orders the chef has spoken and then checked, and inFlow handles stock and sales orders as before.

@graph.name: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than inFlow Inventory?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not overall. We do better with one kind of customer: the chef who keeps calling because browsing a catalog for a known order feels slow. Stock counts, Showroom orders and all the work once you have the order belong to inFlow, so we sit beside it as an addition, not an inFlow Inventory alternative.

@graph.name: Doesn't inFlow's Showroom already end phone orders?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can, for the customers who take to it. Showroom gives each one a private catalog with its own prices and live stock, a cart and a checkout. A kitchen that will not shop for its order that way tends to keep calling. For that kitchen, our app offers a different habit: speak the list, review it, send.

@graph.name: Can our restaurant customers order through inFlow's mobile app or its AI?

acceptedAnswer.text: inFlow built both for your team. Its mobile app gives each team member a login to make sales, check stock, pick and receive. Its built-in AI writes reports on request, and through its MCP server, a link for outside AI tools, an AI assistant can raise an order that someone on your team asks for. Its API also lets other speech or AI order tools be built or connected, so ours is not the only way. What we add is a ready-made app on the chef's own phone, holding only that restaurant's guide, with every item reviewed before it is sent.

@graph.name: Can inFlow Inventory and VoiceOrder Solutions be linked, and does my team still key in orders?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not directly. The two come from different companies, nothing joins them out of the box, and each company answers only for its own product. If your inFlow account is able to accept orders by EDI or through an API, they can land there with no retyping; a demo will tell you whether yours does. By email, it lands as a file in the inbox, every item already reviewed by the chef, and one of your people keys it in from there, not from a call or a voicemail.

@graph.name: How quickly are we set up, and what will it cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most distributors it takes 24 to 48 hours, and nothing in inFlow changes for it. inFlow lists its plan prices on its website; ours are not published, and each distributor gets a quote. A true inFlow Inventory replacement would first have to take over your products, customers and sales history. We start from a single export and leave that history in inFlow.

@graph.name: Do invoices and card payments change?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. inFlow still invoices each order and, in the US and Canada, can take card payments through inFlow Pay. We send you only the order; billing and getting paid are still handled in inFlow.

@graph.name: Where do the inFlow details on this page come from?

acceptedAnswer.text: From inflowinventory.com and inFlow's Learning Center, as we found them on 9 November 2026: the homepage, the inFlow Inventory, Showroom, wholesale, sales, mobile, integrations, pricing and onboarding pages, and inFlow's own comparison pages. Its prices are public; we left the figures off because they change. The note on other tools comes from a web search for inFlow ordering add-ons. Spot anything out of date and we will update it.
